value.first: At 6 months he's right on time - start now if he sits up in the high chair and leans in for food. I'd use iron-first solids with early-and-often allergens, the Health Canada and CPS approach: his stored iron runs low now, and big trials found early, regular peanut cut peanut allergy by roughly 80%. Day 1: a spoon or two of iron-fortified cereal mixed with milk, or mashed lentils. Most lands on the tray - that's a win.
value.second: Days 2-7: iron-rich food twice a day, plus mashed veg and fruit; milk continues as usual. Week 2, peanut: one morning, thin half a teaspoon of smooth peanut butter with warm water, give a tiny taste, wait about 10 minutes, then the rest, and watch him for two hours. A day or two later, well-cooked egg the same way. Then yogurt, wheat, tofu, tahini, fish, one new one a day. Keep each about twice a week after.
value.third: Gagging is noisy and normal; choking is silent. Aim for lumpy and soft finger foods by 9 months, and no honey before 12 months. If a food brings hives or vomiting, stop it and see your provider before offering it again. If you'd rather skip purees, baby-led weaning works with the same allergen schedule. I'll check in Friday.
